title: Colored Dominoes
statementMd:
Manuel loves puzzles and is trying to solve one involving a row of 𝑛n dominoes, each placed vertically. Initially, the positions are numbered from 11 to 𝑛n from left to right.

The domino initially at position 𝑖i has number 𝑎𝑖ai on its upper half and number 𝑏𝑖bi on its lower half. Across all 2𝑛2n halves, each integer from 11 to 2𝑛2n appears exactly once.

Each domino also has a color, represented by an integer. The domino initially at position 𝑖i has color 𝑐𝑖ci. Manuel may perform either of the following operations any number of times:

- Choose a domino and swap the numbers on its upper and lower halves.
- Choose two dominoes of the same color and swap their positions in the row.

His goal is to arrange the dominoes so that, when read from left to right, both the upper numbers and the lower numbers form strictly increasing sequences.

Before performing any operations, Manuel may repaint some dominoes. Each repainted domino may be assigned any integer color from 11 to 𝑛n.

Determine the minimum number of dominoes he must repaint to solve the puzzle. If it is impossible regardless of which dominoes he repaints and which colors he chooses, print −1−1.

## Input

The first line contains an integer 𝑡t (1≤𝑡≤1041≤t≤104), the number of test cases.

Each test case consists of four lines.

The first contains an integer 𝑛n (1≤𝑛≤1061≤n≤106), the number of dominoes.

The second contains 𝑛n integers 𝑎1,…,𝑎𝑛a1,…,an (1≤𝑎𝑖≤2𝑛1≤ai≤2n), the initial upper numbers.

The third contains 𝑛n integers 𝑏1,…,𝑏𝑛b1,…,bn (1≤𝑏𝑖≤2𝑛1≤bi≤2n), the initial lower numbers.

Together, 𝑎a and 𝑏b form a permutation of the integers from 11 to 2𝑛2n.

The fourth contains 𝑛n integers 𝑐1,…,𝑐𝑛c1,…,cn (1≤𝑐𝑖≤𝑛1≤ci≤n), the initial colors.

The sum of 𝑛n over all test cases does not exceed 106106.

## Output

For each test case, print the minimum number of dominoes Manuel must repaint on a separate line, or −1−1 if the goal is impossible.

## Note

**Explanation for example 1**

In the first test case, Manuel can repaint dominoes 22 and 44 with color 11. All dominoes then have the same color, so any two may be swapped. After swapping and flipping some dominoes, he can obtain 1,2,3,4,51,2,3,4,5 on the upper halves and 6,7,8,9,106,7,8,9,10 on the lower halves. The minimum cost is 22.

In the second test case, it is impossible to make both rows increasing, even if all dominoes could be freely rearranged. The answer is therefore −1−1.
